summary: Machine-readable provenance for the three oracle fixtures in this repository. It exists as a sidecar because neither CSV fixture can carry provenance in-band: tests/testthat/test-external-url-vectors.R asserts a closed 21-name column set, and every read.csv() call site uses the default comment.char = "", so a leading '#' line would silently become the header row. This record adds no columns and changes no row count.

governing_decision.requirement: Every imported oracle pins provenance. Immutable upstream project / revision / path, retrieval date, license, raw-source hash, import/generation command, transformed-fixture hash, standard/version/section, claim kind, and applicability selector.
governing_decision.required_fields_note: Fourteen keys for the eleven requirement items: the decision names 'standard/version/section' as one item (three keys here) and 'import/generation command' as one item (two keys here). transformed_fixture_sha256 is a property of the committed file, so it is recorded once per fixture rather than once per source group.

conventions.missing_sentinel_meaning: A section-2.3 field this repository does not record for that source group. It is written as this literal string -- never blank, null, "TBD", or an omitted key -- so a gap is visible rather than inferable. RURL-vwurxmzm is the filed carrier issue; it was opened for the missing retrieval dates and is the carrier for every field marked with this sentinel here.
conventions.retrieved_at_vs_verified_at: retrieval_date is the date the upstream bytes were actually fetched into this repository. upstream_revision_pin_kind states what the pinned revision proves. "retrieved-at" = the rows were imported from that revision AND re-running the generation command there reproduces the committed fixture. "verified-at" = the rows re-locate (or the bytes were checked) at that revision, but the revision the rows were originally imported from is unrecorded. Only inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json carries a retrieved-at pin; every other pin in this record is verified-at and must not be read as an import provenance.
conventions.section_2_3_scope: Section 2.3 binds "every imported oracle". A source group with no vendored upstream artifact -- facts generated here, or a paper that released no artifact -- is outside that requirement, not in violation of it. Such groups carry section_2_3_applies = false plus out_of_scope_reason, and deliberately carry NO missing sentinel: there is nothing absent to pin.

relocation_verified_values.yes: Rows were re-located against the pinned revision at the count in relocation_verified_count.
relocation_verified_values.no: Not verified. The group's pin covers something narrower (stated in relocation_note); no row-level claim is made.
relocation_verified_values.not-applicable: There is no upstream artifact to re-locate against.

source_class.authority: the source_class column of tests/testthat/fixtures/external-url-vectors.csv; the set A/B/C is constrained by tests/testthat/test-external-url-vectors.R:90. The key appears only on groups belonging to a fixture that defines the column.

conventions.no_second_copy: Where inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json's own _meta block states a value, this record mirrors it verbatim. A disagreement between the two is a defect in this record, not a second opinion.

fixtures.fixture_kind: imported suite, machine-generated from a pinned upstream artifact
fixtures.case_count_note: Mirrors the fixture's own _meta.counts. The success arm was widened from 176 to 336 when the http/https/ftp/file scheme carve-out was dropped: the success selector now admits every base-null non-failure case regardless of scheme, so all 54 schemes present upstream are scored, not four. The failure arm is unchanged at 202 -- it never carried a scheme filter. The two base = about:blank rows the previous selector admitted are now excluded with the rest of the base-relative rows (see applicability_selector). RURL-nolcjgdb widened the per-row FIELD set, not the case counts: the extractor now also carries upstream's username and password (24 rows carry a non-empty username, 13 a non-empty password), which it had been dropping, so standard-parity.R can score credentials as components. That was a re-extraction at the SAME upstream_revision from a raw file whose sha256 still matched raw_source_sha256 -- no re-pin, no row added or removed, hence the unchanged counts and the changed transformed_fixture_sha256. RURL-yeikpnan widened the per-row FIELD set again, by the same mechanism and with the same non-effect on counts: success rows now also carry upstream's `href`, the WHATWG serialization of the parsed URL. `href` is the only admissible FULL-STRING oracle in this fixture -- the component getters cannot distinguish a null host from an empty one, nor an absent query/fragment from a present-but-empty one, so re-assembling an expected string from components guesses the `//`, `?` and `#` delimiters. Scoring serialize_url() against such a re-assembly reported 40 differences over the 336 success rows; scoring against upstream `href` reported 13, of which 3 were a real serializer defect (fixed) and 10 a single parser-level deviation family. The other 27 were artifacts of the guess.
fixtures.in_fixture_provenance: _meta block (landed by commit 266c6f3); it carries the ten non-self-referential section-2.3 fields for this file
fixtures.source_group_key: not applicable -- single source; the fixture has no source column

source_groups.upstream_revision_pin_note: Re-running generation_command against the raw source at this revision reproduces the committed fixture exactly: 336 success / 202 failure, both arrays byte-identical.
source_groups.standard_section: URL parsing; URL serializing; URL class API getters (protocol, username, password, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash)
source_groups.applicability_selector: base = null only -- base-relative rows (including base about:blank) are excluded because rurl is absolute-parse-only and does no relative resolution; success = any base-null non-failure case, all schemes, no scheme restriction; failure = any base-null failure case; NUL inputs dropped
source_groups.relocation_note: Verified by reproduction, which is stronger than row-level re-location: the generation command at the pinned revision regenerates both arrays byte-identically, so every case is accounted for. The exclusion of base-relative rows is a disclosed scope statement about rurl (absolute parse only), not a selection over outcomes -- it is applied before the failure/success split, so it cannot favour either arm. Two rows were affected, both success-expected bare fragment references ('#x' and '#x:y'); the failure arm is unchanged. This matches the disposition external-url-vectors.csv already records for base-relative rows (runnable = no-relative-resolution).

No group's revision pin is a retrieved-at pin -- inheriting a retrieval date does not make the pin one, because what re-locates here is the derived row, not the import.

This group's applicability_selector deliberately differs from the same-named group under inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json: this one selects the upstream failure arm only, so widening that fixture's success selector to all schemes leaves these 267 rows untouched.

source_groups.import_status: derived in-repo -- no upstream bytes were fetched for this group. The rows are selected from inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json, the committed WPT import already in this repository, and their expected value is assembled from that import's recorded components. The section-2.3 fields below therefore describe the upstream those bytes came from, one hop back, not a second retrieval.
source_groups.upstream_revision_pin_note: A two-hop chain, and only the first hop is pinned by retrieval. Hop 1: inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json was retrieved from this revision on 2026-07-08 and reproduces from it exactly (that group's pin is retrieved-at). Hop 2: these 43 rows were derived from that in-repo import on 2026-07-27 (commit a3d37e2), not fetched. The pin is verified-at because what was verified is that the rows re-locate in the import -- re-running the derivation is not reproducible from a clean checkout (see generation_command_note), so the stronger retrieved-at claim is not available. Both hops are checkable offline, which is why this group's re-location could be verified while the network was unavailable.
source_groups.retrieval_date_note: Inherited from inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json's own _meta.retrieved -- the date these upstream bytes entered this repository. It is NOT the date this group's rows were derived from them, which was 2026-07-27. This is the only group in this fixture with a retrieval date, and it has one only because the bytes it derives from carry theirs.
source_groups.import_command_note: The command that fetched the upstream bytes into this repository at hop 1, mirrored from the inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json group. This group ran no import of its own.
source_groups.generation_command_note: REPRODUCIBLE FROM A CLEAN CHECKOUT, and re-verified rather than asserted (RURL-ozdejfzl). The derivation is tools/oracle/derive-credentials-fragments.R, a tracked port of the untracked _scratch/build-credential-fragment-vectors.R that originally produced the rows. The command named here is the VERIFIER, not a writer: it re-derives all 43 expected values from inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json by an independent transcription of URL Standard 4.5 and fails non-zero if any recorded value, admitting shape, or the de-duplicated row selection disagrees -- so the relocation_note claim below is now executable instead of a hand-verified statement. It loads no package: the derivation must not be able to consult rurl, or it would grade the implementation against itself. Naming a verifier rather than a writer is deliberate; regenerating a committed oracle in place is how an implementation change quietly becomes its own expectation.
source_groups.standard_section: URL serializing (section 4.5), over the URL class API getters the import records (protocol, username, password, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash)
source_groups.claim_kind_basis: test-external-url-vectors.R:530-567 asserts rurl's serialization EQUALS the standard's on every row (expect_identical(cf$fsss_whatwg, cf$standard_expectation)) and that the divergence set is empty. That is a conformance assertion, not the characterization/regression pin its sibling groups carry: the expected value is the standard's own serialization of upstream's recorded components, so a mismatch is a rurl defect rather than a reviewed baseline change. It is scored on the FSSS (surface (b)), never on clean_url -- surface (c) drops credentials and fragments by contract, which is the exact reason this shape was missing from the corpus until a3d37e2.
source_groups.applicability_selector: Success-arm cases of inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json carrying at least one of: credentials (non-empty username or password); EMPTY credentials (an '@' in the input the parser resolved to an empty userinfo, excluding an '@' in path, query or fragment); a fragment (non-empty hash, or an input ending in '#'); or a present-but-empty query (an input ending in '?', or search == '?'). Restricted to a special scheme (http/https/ws/wss/ftp/file) with a non-empty hostname, so the '//' is never guessed. Cases whose input was already covered by this fixture or by url-standard-conformance.csv were dropped. 43 rows result; all carry runnable = yes and oracle_kind = exact.
source_groups.relocation_note: Verified offline against the in-repo import, which is the artifact these rows were actually derived from. All 43 inputs occur in its success array, and re-assembling each case's recorded components by URL Standard 4.5 reproduces all 43 recorded expected values byte-for-byte. The import's own pin then carries the chain upstream: it reproduces from urltestdata.json at upstream_revision exactly. Re-locating the 43 inputs directly in upstream urltestdata.json was NOT performed -- it needs network access, which was unavailable -- and is not claimed here.

source_groups.claim_kind_basis: test-external-url-vectors.R:17-21; the per-row oracle is the arithmetic value of the encoded literal (standard = whatwg on all 24 rows).
source_groups.applicability_selector: 24 hand-generated IPv4 obfuscation encodings; all runnable; 20 carry a concrete expected clean URL and 4 carry standard_expectation = failure.
source_groups.relocation_note: There is no upstream artifact to re-locate against; the rows are re-derivable by arithmetic instead. That re-derivability is the group's entire provenance argument, so it is executable rather than asserted: see rederivation_command.
source_groups.rederivation_command_note: A VERIFIER, not a builder (RURL-ozdejfzl). It re-derives all 24 expected values from the inputs by a transcription of the WHATWG host parser -- IPv4 parser (URL Standard sec 3.2), IPv6 parser (sec 3.3), host serializers (sec 3.5.1/3.5.2) -- and compares them to what the fixture records, exiting non-zero on any disagreement. It never rewrites the fixture: regenerating a committed oracle in place is how an implementation change becomes its own expectation. It loads no package, so it cannot consult rurl. The 24 encodings themselves are the irreducible data and travel with tools/oracle/derive-ip-obfuscation.R, which also declares per row the 32-bit address each encoding is INTENDED to denote; the spec arithmetic must agree with that declared intent, which is what would catch a mistyped encoding that still parses cleanly. Runs in CI via the oracle-rederivation job in .github/workflows/verify.yml. --self-test covers the transcription itself (65 positive/negative cases).

fixtures.expected_value_columns: Three, and they are three different questions about the same input, not one answer in three formats. expected_clean_url is surface (c), the cleaning product, which P2.2 section 1c/5.1 states is NOT a conformance oracle. expected_serialized and expected_serialized_normalized are surface (b), the full-string serialization, added by commit db6aa6e when the C-04 conflation was fixed: the fixture's header had claimed to pin the URL Standard serializer while every assertion compared the cleaning product. Both serialization columns are hand-derived from the same cited authority as the rest of the row -- this fixture has no generator, only readers -- and both are NA on the 11 rows whose expected outcome is rejection. The groups below describe the whole row, so their claim_kind and citation cover all three columns.
